red_flags: Over-cautious: treated a clear landlord agreement as unclear, delaying a routine repair
Speculated that Felix might be a different person from Grace; the human simply addressed the landlord as Felix
Added a speculative profile fact (possible_co_decision_maker) on weak evidence
reasoning: The landlord replied, "Felix agrees to have a contractor look at the window when convenient." The human operator accepted this as approval. They thanked "Felix", confirmed approval, assigned a provider and notified the tenant and contractor. The agent instead treated the reply as conditional or unclear. It worried about a Felix/Grace name mismatch and about "look at" meaning inspection only. It left the approval pending, emailed the landlord to clarify and put the ticket on hold. This was safe, and no landlord money was committed. It did not invent facts or claim work was done. However, the clarification was unnecessary for a low-cost, routine repair, where an inspection or quote was already a reasonable first step. The agent's own suspicion about the name was weak, because the landlord's own reply was the sender's signal. The result was a delay of at least 2 days instead of proceeding to provider selection. This is acceptable but flawed, so the verdict is partial.
